!52 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// This is the shader from issue 3414, unmodified, at the profile used in the thread.\0A//\0A// In each pane, compare the last argument of the \22call void @dx.op.traceRay\22 line with the\0A// payload parameter named in the \22define void @...main...\22 line at the top of the function.\0A//\0A// In the DXC 1.6.2112 and DXC 1.8.2502 panes those two are the same value: the recursive\0A// TraceRay is handed the closest-hit shader's own inout payload object, so the caller and the\0A// recursive call share one payload instead of the copy that HLSL copy-in/copy-out requires.\0A//\0A// In the DXC 1.8.2505 and trunk panes the TraceRay argument is a separate local allocation\0A// instead, written on the line immediately before the call and read back immediately after it.\0A// That is the copy-in/copy-out, and it is exactly what the reporter's workaround forced by hand\0A// by introducing a second Payload variable.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A#define RECURSION_DEPTH 30\0A#define BUGGED 1\0A\0Astruct !52 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// This is the shader from issue 3414, unmodified, at the profile used in the thread.\0A//\0A// In each pane, compare the last argument of the \22call void @dx.op.traceRay\22 line with the\0A// payload parameter named in the \22define void @...main...\22 line at the top of the function.\0A//\0A// In the DXC 1.6.2112 and DXC 1.8.2502 panes those two are the same value: the recursive\0A// TraceRay is handed the closest-hit shader's own inout payload object, so the caller and the\0A// recursive call share one payload instead of the copy that HLSL copy-in/copy-out requires.\0A//\0A// In the DXC 1.8.2505 and trunk panes the TraceRay argument is a separate local allocation\0A// instead, written on the line immediately before the call and read back immediately after it.\0A// That is the copy-in/copy-out, and it is exactly what the reporter's workaround forced by hand\0A// by introducing a second Payload variable.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A#define RECURSION_DEPTH 30\0A#define BUGGED 1\0A\0Astruct Payload {\0A    uint4 data0;\0A};\0A\0ARaytracingAccelerationStructure tlas : register(t0, space0);\0A\0A[shader(\22closesthit\22)] void\0Amain(inout Payload payload, in BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes attribs) {\0A    float3 dir = WorldRayDirection();\0A\0A    RayDesc ray;\0A    ray.Origin = WorldRayOrigin() + dir * RayTCurrent();\0A    ray.TMin = 0.1;\0A    ray.Direction = float3(dir.x, dir.y, -dir.z);\0A    ray.TMax = 1000.0;\0A\0A#if BUGGED\0A    payload.data0 += uint4(1,1,1,1);\0A\0A    if (payload.data0.x < RECURSION_DEPTH) {\0A }\0A#else\0A    Payload new_payload;\0A    new_payload = payload;\0A    new_payload.data0 += uint4(1,1,1,1);\0A\0A    if (new_payload.data0.x < RECURSION_DEPTH) {\0A        TraceRay(tlas,\0A !52 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// This is the shader from issue 3414, unmodified, at the profile used in the thread.\0A//\0A// In each pane, compare the last argument of the \22call void @dx.op.traceRay\22 line with the\0A// payload parameter named in the \22define void @...main...\22 line at the top of the function.\0A//\0A// In the DXC 1.6.2112 and DXC 1.8.2502 panes those two are the same value: the recursive\0A// TraceRay is handed the closest-hit shader's own inout payload object, so the caller and the\0A// recursive call share one payload instead of the copy that HLSL copy-in/copy-out requires.\0A//\0A// In the DXC 1.8.2505 and trunk panes the TraceRay argument is a separate local allocation\0A// instead, written on the line immediately before the call and read back immediately after it.\0A// That is the copy-in/copy-out, and it is exactly what the reporter's workaround forced by hand\0A// by introducing a second Payload variable.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A#define RECURSION_DEPTH 30\0A#define BUGGED 1\0A\0Astruct Payload {\0A    uint4 data0;\0A};\0A\0ARaytracingAccelerationStructure tlas : register(t0, space0);\0A\0A[shader(\22closesthit\22)] void\0Amain(inout Payload payload, in BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes attribs) {\0A    float3 dir = WorldRayDirection();\0A\0A    RayDesc ray;\0A    ray.Origin = WorldRayOrigin() + dir * RayTCurrent();\0A    ray.TMin = 0.1;\0A    ray.Direction = float3(dir.x, dir.y, -dir.z);\0A    ray.TMax = 1000.0;\0A\0A#if BUGGED\0A    payload.data0 += uint4(1,1,1,1);\0A\0A    if (payload.data0.x < RECURSION_DEPTH) {\0A        TraceRay(tlas,\0A                RAY_FLAG_FORCE_OPAQUE | RAY_FLAG_CULL_BACK_FACING_TRIANGLES |\0A                    0, // flags\0A                0xff,  // instance inclusion mask\0A                0,     // RayContributionToHitGroupIndex\0A                1,     // MultiplierForGeometryContributionToHitGroupIndex\0A                0,     // MissShaderIndex\0A                ray, payload);\0A    }\0A#else\0A    Payload new_payload;\0A    new_payload = payload;\0A    new_payload.data0 += uint4(1,1,1,1);\0A\0A    if (new_payload.data0.x < RECURSION_DEPTH) {\0A        TraceRay(tlas,\0A                 RAY_FLAG_FORCE_OPAQUE | RAY_FLAG_CULL_BACK_FACING_TRIANGLES |\0A                     0, // flags\0A                 0xff,  // instance inclusion mask\0A                 0,     // RayContributionToHitGroupIndex\0A                 1,     // MultiplierForGeometryContributionToHitGroupIndex\0A                 0,     // MissShaderIndex\0A                 ray, new_payload);\0A\0A
